comment: The error was treating D’s roughly 3× calibrated progress advantage as decisive. On this identical normalized residual ReLU network, RMSprop B and Adam E achieve lower short-budget CE than momentum SGD D. Coordinatewise adaptation is a plausible explanation, not a measured mechanism. K1012 explicitly warns that such progress gaps are inconclusive; K1003/K1019 were overextended. K1070 supports B over E. A proposed adaptive-over-D rule failed backtesting: relevant history favored SGD in 2/2 comparisons; mixed-architecture XOR lab comparisons favored adaptive in only 5/31 pairs across 15 sets. The two exact-model T256 lab pairs also favored SGD, on different architectures. Thus this gold establishes a recipe-local exception, not a general optimizer reversal.

XOR binary classification on tabular features. Features are drawn i.i.d. from a standard normal; the label depends on the *sign agreement* of two active coordinates, so no linear function of the inputs separates the classes at all — a model must compose the two coordinates multiplicatively. Any remaining coordinates are pure distractors. The dataset card below states the active coordinates and the exact label rule. Every candidate trains on the same materialized train/test splits.

### Data-generating and classification rule
- Rule family: `xor`; active coordinates: `x_5`, `x_8`
- Feature distribution: every coordinate is sampled independently from `Normal(0, 1)`.

- Label rule: `y = 1` exactly when `s(x) > 0`; otherwise `y = 0`.
- XOR interpretation: `x` is class 1 exactly when its two active coordinates have opposite signs, and class 0 when they share a sign.
- Bayes decision boundary: `s(x) = 0`; labels are an exact function of `x`, so this boundary is attainable.
- Threshold calibration: `0` was chosen from 4096 independent calibration rows as the closest round value to the 50% quantile of `s(x)`; on those 4096 rows it labels 49.7% of them class 1.
- Reproducibility: point seed `12000403263150`, calibration seed `12000403264150`.
